ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$6.74 (seg2 extra_km 4.78 × S$1.4100/km) to the rider as a Ryde voucher; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file for the 19:03–19:12 unexplained deviation.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the two chat messages [F9][F10] concern a route proposal only; the driver's post-trip statement [F12] and the complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. Nothing to escalate on SAFE-1/SAFE-2.

Service type: RydeTAXI (metered), so a route deviation that adds distance adds fare (policy §0; RD-2 RydeTAXI branch, unit rate S$1.4100/km from F5). Two off-route segments are on the table and each is reviewed separately under RD-1.

Segment A [F3] 18:46–18:56, +5.66 km: the driver proposed before leaving the optimal route to go round the jam via Rifle Range Road [F9, 18:42], the rider agreed 18:43 [F10] and that agreement precedes the segment start (18:46) → RD-5 satisfied. The rider's complaint itself concedes this leg ("I agreed to go round the jam near the start"). The stated reason is a jam on the BKE, and the traffic fact shows BKE at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) in the trip window [F13], but band 4 is not band 1–2 and there is no incident record [F15], so RD-4 does not exempt it — the consent under RD-5 does. Finding: exempt.

Segment B [F4] 19:03–19:12, +4.78 km: no chat message covers it (the record has exactly two messages, both about the first reroute) [F11], so there is no rider consent for this segment. The driver's statement calls it "my GPS rerouting" [F12]; a driver's own account cannot convert an unreserved segment into an exempt one and he named no alternative road, so the reading is that the segment counts (RD-1). RD-4 fails as well: no traffic incident on the optimal route [F15], and the only band facts are band 4 [F13][F14], which cannot exempt a segment on their own (RD-4(b)). Finding: counts.

Amount [RD-2]: refund = Σ(unexempt segment extra_km) × this trip's per-km rate = 4.78 km × S$1.4100/km = S$6.7398 → S$6.74. Only the metered distance unit is refunded; the trip's other excess mileage (the unattributed remainder between the billed 10.38 km and the segment sums, F1/F5) is not refundable, and the waiting charge F6 (S$0.11, 0.4 min of meter waiting, and the segment's stop time) is not refunded under RD-2/RD-3(c). Rider is not the party at fault, so no account flag on the rider; the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 d [F18], so RD-6's "repeated" condition is not met and flag_account is not applied.

Evidence status: sufficient — GPS segments are timed, the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F11], and the fare breakdown gives the per-km rate [F5].

segment_findings.reason: RD-5 / RD-3(a): the driver proposed routing around the BKE jam via Rifle Range Road at 18:42 before leaving the optimal route, and the rider's own timestamped message agreed at 18:43, i.e. before the segment start 18:46; the rider's complaint concedes this leg. The chat is complete and every message is timestamped [F11].

RD-1 / RD-5: no chat message covers this 19:03–19:12 segment — the record holds only the two messages about the first reroute; the driver's post-trip claim of GPS rerouting is a statement only and names no road, so nothing ties an agreement to this segment; RD-4 gives no cover either (band 4 traffic only [F13][F14], no incident [F15]). The S$14.64 (10.38 km) excess billed [F5] is 5.66 + 4.78 km, plus 0.06 km matching noise; the 0.06 km and the noise-tolerance mileage are not refundable, only the 4.78 km segment, giving 4.78 × S$1.4100 = S$6.74.

Reconsidered under RD-4 as an alternative basis: the stated cause was congestion on the BKE, and the traffic fact confirms BKE at speed band 4 in the trip window. Band 4 is not band 1–2 and there is no incident record [F15], so RD-4 does not by itself exempt the segment — the exemption rests on RD-5 consent. The amount is unaffected; the only change would be the grounds.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's statement that 'the rider agreed' and that the second turn-off was GPS rerouting: a verbal/claimed agreement not present in the chat is not consent under RD-5 (G11), and the chat record [F11] shows only the first reroute was discussed. The driver also names no road for the second segment, so no record ties it to any agreed route (RD-5, G13).

BKE speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) used as a stand-alone excuse: RD-4 requires band 1–2 and/or an incident on the replaced optimal-route segment within the window; band 4 is congestion, not a 'reasonable cause' strong enough to exempt a deviation on its own (RD-4(b)).
PIE speed band 4: unrelated to either off-route segment and not tied to the replaced optimal-route stretch; no exemption follows.
Rider's implicit request for the whole excess: an RD-2 refund covers only unexempt segment extra_km; the 0.06 km unattributed difference and the 0.4 min meter waiting charge stay with the rider.
